status_summary: Executive Order 14164 (2025-01-20) and Bondi's 2025-02-05 memo lifted the federal execution moratorium and directed prosecutors to seek death in specified categories, including murders of law enforcement officers and capital crimes by people in the country illegally. On 2026-04-24 DOJ announced it had authorized seeking death against 44 defendants, readopted the pentobarbital protocol, directed the Bureau of Prisons to add other execution methods including the firing squad, and planned rules on habeas review and clemency petitions. Executive Order 14164 states that President Biden commuted 37 of the 40 federal death sentences on 2024-12-23 and directs a review of those offenders' conditions of confinement. The Bureau of Prisons history page lists no federal execution after 2021-01-16.

timeline.event: Executive Order 14164, Restoring the Death Penalty and Protecting Public Safety, signed (Federal Register 2025-01-30): directs the Attorney General to pursue capital punishment, seek death in specified cases, assist states with execution drugs, and seek reversal of precedents limiting capital punishment.

Bondi memo lifts the 2021 execution moratorium, directs prosecutors to seek death for the most serious provable offenses, orders review of earlier no-seek decisions within 120 days, and directs the Office of Legal Policy to assess readopting the single-drug pentobarbital protocol.

DOJ announces it has authorized seeking death against 44 defendants (nine personally by Acting AG Blanche), readopted the pentobarbital protocol, directed the Bureau of Prisons to expand methods (including the firing squad) and examine facility changes, and prepared a legislative proposal, with rulemaking on habeas and clemency to follow.

title: Enforce the federal death penalty and seek finality for capital cases
